topic: Pure Fourier Series: Decoding the Rhythm of Signals

sections.title: The Hook: The Symphony of Waves
lecture_lines: Complex signals are sums of simple sine waves.
See the waveform break into individual clean waves.
Nature's rhythm is built from simple periodic parts.
animations: Decompose complex wave into 3 simple sine waves.
Animate 3 simple waves merging into complex signal.

sections.title: Mathematical Framework: The Harmonic Foundation
lecture_lines: Fourier series decomposes signals into harmonic components.
Coefficients determine the weight of each component.
Watch the square wave form, piece by piece.
Harmonics build the signal's unique profile.
Integration reveals the amplitude of every frequency.
animations: Display Fourier formula: f(t) = Σ c_n e^{inωt} in #00FF00.
Animate coefficients c_n values scaling bars.
Animate square wave construction by adding N harmonics.
Visualize frequency components appearing as bars in spectrum.
Show integration process calculating a single coefficient.

sections.title: Visualization: The Epicycles Construction
lecture_lines: Rotating vectors trace complex paths easily.
Epicycles add layers to create shapes.
Observe the Fourier robot drawing patterns.
Circles define the rhythm of the motion.
Geometry turns abstract math into clear visualization.
animations: Draw rotating vector (radius 2) at origin in #FF00FF.

sections.title: Application: Why it Matters
lecture_lines: Fourier transforms are essential for noise cancellation.
Compression algorithms use frequencies to store images.
Technology relies on splitting signals into components.
animations: Display noisy signal, highlight high frequency components in #FF0000.
Remove high frequency components to show noise cancellation.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
lecture_lines: Fourier series acts as a frequency prism.
Time and frequency domains represent signal data.
Analyze complex patterns by splitting them apart.
